The lines inside a group measure nearly the same thing, so groups are counted, not lines; a group reads tight or loose only when more than half of its lines do. Fund positioning is sentiment: it reads loose and is shown but not counted. Each line states its threshold and, where eight years of history exist, how often it has read tight and loose, so a line that usually fires can be discounted. It covers the futures curves and US data, not the world balance, and it is not a forecast. Whether a high crack spread is evidence of crude tightness is a judgement, not a threshold. Without that line, refining demand reads tight and the evidence points to a tight market, so today's verdict does not depend on it.

readings.note: Hypothetical. The stated changes are applied to the 2027-01 futures prices of 2026-11-20 and the score is recomputed against the same history; the curve is left as it is. In the scenario the score tilts against US crude exports. A price indicator, not an executable arbitrage. +2 = wide spread, cheap freight, contango; -2 = narrow spread, dear freight, backwardation. The spread is Brent minus WTI on futures of one delivery month, ranked against that contract pair's own history (up to three years). Freight is the Breakwave tanker ETF, a proxy, not a route rate; no physical differentials or port costs are included.
